sources.quote: The modal verbs (can, could, may, might, mote, must, shall, should, will, would, and dare, need and ought when included) form a subclass of auxiliary verbs.

The modal verbs (can, could, may, might, mote, must, shall, should, will, would, and dare, need and ought when included) form a subclass of auxiliary verbs.

notes: Fictional relation in TBox: a real class (English auxiliary verbs) with a made-up property (a mark in an invented notation). Well-known members are determinate here: the property is fictional, so no stored fact about 'might', 'has', 'will' or 'do' competes with the rule (README, Insert: relation inserts may have all derived queries determinate). Q1 goes through the real subclass modal ⊑ auxiliary; Q3 adds a rule stated in the prompt. Examples avoid 'have' and 'do' as main verbs (the R1 trap: 'She has a car').
